reviews.decision_reason: demand_selection passes every corpus row through because all supplied demand_score values are >=3, including records that later remain unsupported by capability evidence. Under the strict market-demand review criteria, numeric scores and need labels alone do not establish observed demand, and selecting unsupported candidates is behaviorally significant because it preserves n06-r01 and n06-r07 as demand-backed needs for downstream prioritization.

evidence_normalization retains all eight selected rows by an allow-list rather than validating that each need is supported by observed demand evidence. This perpetuates unsupported candidates, but the supplied boundary evidence shows it received already-selected rows from demand_selection, so it is secondary rather than the first localized fault.

provenance_assembly deterministically ranks the retained rows by demand_score and record_id, producing n06-r01 as rank 1. That ranking is deterministic but demand_score is not sufficient market-demand evidence under the review criteria, so this boundary amplifies the unsupported selection into provenance ranks used downstream. The evidence does not show provenance_assembly introduced the unsupported candidates, so it is not the primary localized fault.
